definition_zh: 骑手；骑马的人；附加条款
definition_en: a person who rides a horse or bicycle, or an extra clause added to a document
core_image: 草原上勒住缰绳的骑手
scene: 草原上，骑手勒住缰绳让马慢慢停下。The rider pulled the reins and slowed the horse.
sceneCN: 这里 rider 是「骑手」（第 1 个义项：骑马或骑车的人）；句意：草原上，骑手勒住缰绳让马慢慢停下。

pos.zh: 骑手；骑马的人；附加条款

senses.title: A person on horseback
senses.definition: a person who rides a horse
senses.example: The rider guided the horse across the field.
senses.exampleCN: 骑手引导马穿过田野。
senses.why: Ride plus -er names the person who rides.
senses.whyCN: ride 加 -er 就指进行骑乘的人。

senses.title: A person on a bike
senses.definition: a person who rides a bicycle or motorcycle
senses.definitionCN: 骑自行车或摩托车的人
senses.example: A rider in a yellow coat passed us.
senses.exampleCN: 一位穿黄外套的骑车人超过我们。
senses.why: The same -er word covers any vehicle you ride.
senses.whyCN: 同一个 -er 后缀也涵盖任何可骑乘的交通工具。

senses.title: An extra clause
senses.definition: an additional condition added to a law or contract
senses.definitionCN: 附加在法律或合同上的额外条件
senses.example: They added a rider to protect the tenants.
senses.exampleCN: 他们增加了一条保护租客的附加条款。
senses.why: A rider travels along with the main document.
senses.whyCN: 附加条款跟随主文件一起同行。

intro.en: Rider is simply ride plus -er, the person who rides.
intro.cn: rider 就是 ride 加 -er，即进行骑乘的人。

items.en: Ridan means to ride.
items.cn: ridan 意为骑乘。

items.en: Ride keeps the old verb.
items.cn: ride 保留了这一古老动词。

items.en: -er marks the person who does it.
items.cn: -er 标记做这件事的人。

items.en: Rider also means an extra clause.
items.cn: rider 也指附加条款。

items.en: The legal sense grows from papers that ride along.
items.cn: 法律义来自随主文件同行的附加页。

note.en: A rider rides; a cyclist is the usual word for a bicycle rider.
note.cn: rider 指骑乘者；cyclist 是骑车人更常用的说法。

entries.definition: to sit on and control a horse or bike
a person who rides a bicycle
a person travelling in a vehicle

normalIntro.en: A rider is the rider on the ride.
normalIntro.cn: rider 就是骑在 ride 上的那个人。

normal.en: Add -er to ride to get rider.
normal.cn: ride 加 -er 就得到 rider。

normal.en: A horse rider holds the reins.
normal.cn: horse rider 握着缰绳。

normal.en: A bicycle rider wears a helmet.
normal.cn: bicycle rider 戴着头盔。

normal.en: A rider to a bill changes the law.
normal.cn: rider to a bill 会改变法律。

normal.en: A free rider pays nothing.
normal.cn: free rider 不付任何代价。

abstract.en: Picture a lone figure on a galloping horse.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孤独的身影骑在飞奔的马上。

abstract.en: Imagine a slip of paper riding along with a contract.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸片跟着合同一起旅行。

abstract.en: Think of a bike light moving through the dark.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏车灯在黑暗中移动。

examples.en: The rider wore a red helmet.
examples.cn: 这位骑车人戴着红色头盔。

examples.en: Every rider must pay for the trip.
examples.cn: 每位乘车人都必须为行程付费。

examples.en: A rider was added to the agreement.
examples.cn: 协议中增加了一条附加条款。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ride（骑）＋ r」——骑在马上的人，就是骑手。

root: ride（骑）＋ -er（人）→ rider，核心义「骑乘的人」；法律义由「随文件同行的附页」引申而来。

sensesIntro.en: A rider can be a person on a horse or bike, or an extra clause attached to a document.
sensesIntro.cn: rider 可以指骑马或骑车的人，也可以指附加在文件上的条款。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure holding reins on a horse.
core.cn: 核心意象：握着缰绳骑在马上的人。

branches.en: The rider on a horse is the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 骑马的人是这个词最古老的义项。

branches.en: The same person word now covers bikes.
branches.cn: 同一个表示人的词如今也涵盖自行车。

branches.en: A clause rides along with the main document.
branches.cn: 附加条款跟着主文件一起走。

branches.en: Both horse and bike riders sit and control.
branches.cn: 骑马与骑车的人都是坐着操控。

branches.en: The person sense and the paper sense share the idea of riding along.
branches.cn: 人义与文件义都共享「随行」的概念。

intro.en: Rider is ride plus the person suffix -er.
intro.cn: rider 是 ride 加表示人的后缀 -er。

latinIntro.en: The word stays close to its Old English verb ridan.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词一直贴近古英语动词 ridan。

items.example: -er turns a verb into a person.
items.exampleCN: -er 把动词变成表示人的名词。

items.example: Free rider adds a social sense.
items.exampleCN: free rider 增加了一层社会含义。

definition_en: a long narrow raised top, as of hills or a roof
core_image: 清晨沿着山脊向上的登山者
scene: 清晨，登山者沿着山脊一步步向最高峰前进。The hikers followed the ridge toward the highest peak.
sceneCN: 这里 ridge 是「山脊」（第 1 个义项：山脉狭长的顶部）；句意：清晨，登山者沿着山脊一步步向最高峰前进。

senses.title: A hilltop line
senses.definition: a long narrow top of a hill or mountain
senses.definitionCN: 山丘或山脉狭长的顶部
senses.example: We walked along the ridge at sunrise.
senses.exampleCN: 日出时我们沿着山脊行走。
senses.why: The ridge is the raised line the hills make.
senses.whyCN: 山脊是群山形成的隆起线条。

senses.title: A raised line
senses.definition: a raised line on a surface
senses.example: A ridge of sand marked the tide line.
senses.exampleCN: 一道沙脊标出了潮水线。
senses.why: Any long raised line looks like a small hill.
senses.whyCN: 任何狭长的隆起都像一座小山。

senses.title: The top of a roof
senses.definition: the highest line where two roof slopes meet
senses.definitionCN: 两片屋顶相交的最高线
senses.example: A bird sat on the ridge of the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 一只鸟停在屋脊上。
senses.why: The roof ridge is the hill of the house.
senses.whyCN: 屋脊就是房子的「山脊」。

intro.en: Ridge comes from Old English hrycg, the back or spine.
intro.cn: ridge 源自古英语 hrycg，意为背部或脊骨。

items.en: Hrycg means the back of a body.
items.cn: hrycg 意为身体的背部。

items.en: The sense moves to the back of a hill.
items.cn: 词义扩展到山的「背脊」。

items.en: It also names the top line of a roof.
items.cn: 它也指屋顶的最高线。

items.en: Ridge covers any long raised line.
items.cn: 如今 ridge 涵盖任何狭长的隆起。

items.en: Weather maps use ridges of high pressure.
items.cn: 天气图用 ridge 表示高压脊。

note.en: A ridge is a line along the top; a crest is the very highest point.
note.cn: ridge 是沿顶部的线，crest 是最高的顶点。

entries.definition: a structure over a river or road
the top of a hill or wave
the line of bones down the back

normalIntro.en: A ridge is the back of a hill.
normalIntro.cn: ridge 就是山的脊背。

normal.en: A mountain ridge is a long high line.
normal.cn: mountain ridge 是一条高高长长的线。

normal.en: The roof ridge is the top of the house.
normal.cn: roof ridge 是房子的最高处。

normal.en: A ridge of sand forms along the shore.
normal.cn: 岸边会形成一道沙脊。

normal.en: Walk along the ridge for the best view.
normal.cn: 沿着山脊走能看到最好的风景。

normal.en: Ridge and back share one old image.
normal.cn: ridge 与背部共享同一个古老意象。

abstract.en: Picture a spine running across the land.
abstract.cn: 想象一根脊骨横贯大地。

abstract.en: Imagine a knife edge of rock against the sky.
abstract.cn: 想象岩壁像刀刃一样切向天空。

abstract.en: Think of a roof line like a hill in miniature.
abstract.cn: 想象屋脊像一座缩小的山。

examples.en: The village lies below the ridge.
examples.cn: 村庄坐落在山脊之下。

examples.en: Wind blew along the ridge all night.
examples.cn: 整夜风都沿着山脊吹。

examples.en: Rain ran down the ridge of the tent.
examples.cn: 雨水顺着帐篷的脊线流下。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ridge」听起来像「立脊」——立起来的脊背，就是山脊。

root: 古英语 hrycg（背脊）→ 山的背脊 → 屋脊与各种隆起，核心义「狭长的隆起线」。

sensesIntro.en: A ridge is the long raised top of hills, or any raised line such as a roof ridge.
sensesIntro.cn: ridge 是山丘狭长的顶部，也可指屋脊等各种隆起线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the spine of a hill.
core.cn: 核心意象：山的脊背。

branches.en: The hill ridge is the oldest landscape sense.
branches.cn: 山脊是最古老的地景义项。

branches.en: Any raised line on a surface borrows the image.
branches.cn: 表面上任何隆起线都借用了这个意象。

branches.en: The roof ridge is the hill of a house.
branches.cn: 屋脊是房子的「山」。

branches.en: Both land and sand form long raised lines.
branches.cn: 陆地和沙地都会形成狭长的隆起线。

branches.en: Hill and roof share one high edge.
branches.cn: 山与屋顶共享同一条高脊。

intro.en: Ridge is a native English word built on the image of a back.
intro.cn: ridge 是英语本族词，建立在「背部」的意象上。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin prefix here; the word descends from Old English hrycg.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁前缀，该词直接源自古英语 hrycg。

items.example: Ridging names the making of ridges.
The compound adds a building sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词增加了建筑含义。

items.example: The compound makes the landscape clear.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词让地貌含义更明确。

definition_en: so silly or unreasonable that it deserves laughter
core_image: 戴着过大的帽子去开会的人
scene: 他戴着一顶过大的帽子走进会场，看上去十分可笑。He wore a huge hat to the meeting and looked ridiculous.
sceneCN: 这里 ridiculous 是「可笑的」（第 1 个义项：荒谬到引人发笑）；句意：他戴着一顶过大的帽子走进会场，看上去十分可笑。

senses.title: Too silly to believe
senses.definition: so silly that it seems impossible
senses.definitionCN: 愚蠢得让人觉得不可能
senses.example: It is ridiculous to blame the rain for your lateness.
senses.exampleCN: 把迟到归咎于下雨实在荒谬。
senses.why: The word comes from laughter at what is absurd.
senses.whyCN: 这个词源于对荒谬之事的发笑。

senses.title: Funny to look at
senses.definition: strange enough to make people laugh
senses.example: He looked ridiculous in that tiny jacket.
senses.exampleCN: 他穿着那件小小的外套显得很可笑。
senses.why: Something badly matched looks laughable.
senses.whyCN: 搭配不当的东西看起来就好笑。

senses.title: Wildly unreasonable
senses.definition: unreasonably large or small
senses.example: They asked a ridiculous price for the old bike.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为那辆旧自行车要了个离谱的价钱。
senses.why: A number beyond sense also earns a laugh.
senses.whyCN: 不合常理的数字同样引人发笑。

intro.en: Ridiculous comes from Latin ridiculus, laughable, from ridere, to laugh.
intro.cn: ridiculous 源自拉丁语 ridiculus（可笑的），来自 ridere（笑）。

items.en: Ridere means to laugh.
items.cn: ridere 意为笑。

items.en: Ridiculus means fit to be laughed at.
items.cn: ridiculus 意为值得被嘲笑的。

items.en: French ridicule carries the sense of mockery.
items.cn: 法语 ridicule 带有嘲弄之意。

items.en: English ridiculous means absurd.
items.cn: 英语 ridiculous 意为荒谬。

items.en: It also scolds wild prices and plans.
items.cn: 如今它也用来批评离谱的价格与计划。

note.en: Ridiculous points to laughter; absurd points to the lack of sense.
note.cn: ridiculous 指向发笑，absurd 指向缺乏道理。

entries.definition: so bad or odd that one laughs

normalIntro.en: Ridiculous describes what deserves a laugh.
normalIntro.cn: ridiculous 形容值得发笑的事。

normal.en: Ridicule is the verb that mocks.
normal.cn: ridicule 是表示嘲笑的动词。

normal.en: A ridiculous idea makes no sense.
normal.cn: ridiculous idea 毫无道理。

normal.en: That hat looks ridiculous on you.
normal.cn: 那顶帽子戴在你头上很可笑。

normal.en: A ridiculous price is far too high.
normal.cn: ridiculous price 高得离谱。

normal.en: Laughter is hidden inside the word.
normal.cn: 笑声藏在这个词里面。

abstract.en: Picture a clown at a serious meeting.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小丑出现在严肃的会议上。

abstract.en: Imagine shoes three sizes too big.
abstract.cn: 想象一双大了三号的鞋。

abstract.en: Think of a price tag with too many zeros.
abstract.cn: 想象一张写着太多零的价签。

examples.en: The plan sounded ridiculous at first.
examples.cn: 这个计划起初听起来很荒唐。

examples.en: It is ridiculous to walk in this storm.
examples.cn: 在这种暴风雨里走路太荒唐了。

examples.en: She felt ridiculous in the wrong uniform.
examples.cn: 穿着错误的制服让她觉得很可笑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ridi（笑）＋ culous」——让人忍不住笑出来的，就是荒谬可笑。

root: 拉丁语 ridere（笑）→ ridiculus（可笑的）→ 法语 ridicule → ridiculous，核心义「荒谬到引人发笑」。

sensesIntro.en: Ridiculous means silly enough to laugh at, funny in appearance, or wildly unreasonable.
sensesIntro.cn: ridiculous 意为愚蠢可笑、模样古怪，或离谱得不合理。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a laugh rising at something absurd.
core.cn: 核心意象：面对荒谬之事升起的笑声。

branches.en: An absurd idea invites laughter.
branches.cn: 荒谬的想法招来笑声。

branches.en: A mismatched outfit looks funny.
branches.cn: 不搭的装扮看起来好笑。

branches.en: A wild price is laughably unreasonable.
branches.cn: 离谱的价格荒唐得可笑。

branches.en: Both a foolish plan and a strange look make us laugh.
branches.cn: 愚蠢的计划与古怪的模样都让人发笑。

branches.en: A funny look and a wild price both break good sense.
branches.cn: 古怪模样与离谱价格都违背常理。

intro.en: Ridiculous grows from the Latin root rid, to laugh.
intro.cn: ridiculous 由拉丁词根 rid（笑）生长而来。

latinIntro.en: Ridere gives ridiculus, and French carries ridicule into English.
latinIntro.cn: ridere 给出 ridiculus，法语又把 ridicule 带进英语。

items.example: Rid carries the idea of laughter.
Ridicule brings the word to English.

latinEntries.example: Ridere is the source of ridiculous.
latinEntries.exampleCN: ridere 是 ridiculous 的来源。

definition_en: a long gun fired from the shoulder, or to search through something quickly
core_image: 士兵倚在墙边擦拭步枪
scene: 士兵把步枪靠在墙边，仔细擦拭长长的枪管。The soldier leaned the rifle against the wall and cleaned the barrel.
sceneCN: 这里 rifle 是「步枪」（第 1 个义项：可从肩上射击的长枪）；句意：士兵把步枪靠在墙边，仔细擦拭长长的枪管。

senses.title: A long gun
senses.definition: a long gun held against the shoulder
senses.example: The guard carried an old rifle.
senses.exampleCN: 卫兵拿着一支旧步枪。
senses.why: The grooved barrel is the heart of a rifle.
senses.whyCN: 带膛线的枪管是步枪的核心。

senses.title: Searching quickly
senses.definition: to search through something in a hurry
senses.example: She rifled through the drawer for her keys.
senses.exampleCN: 她在抽屉里匆忙翻找钥匙。
senses.why: Hurried hands scrape through things like a groove.
senses.whyCN: 匆忙的手像划过沟槽一样翻动东西。

senses.title: Stealing from a place
senses.definition: to search a place and take what is inside
senses.definitionCN: 翻遍某处并拿走里面的东西
senses.example: Thieves had rifled the empty house.
senses.exampleCN: 小偷洗劫了那栋空房子。
senses.why: A quick search can turn into plunder.
senses.whyCN: 快速翻找可能变成掠夺。

intro.en: The gun sense comes from a grooved barrel; the verb comes from Old French rifler, to scratch or plunder.
intro.cn: 枪义来自刻有沟槽的枪管；动词义来自古法语 rifler（抓挠、掠夺）。

items.en: Riffel means a groove cut in metal.
items.cn: riffel 意为金属上刻出的沟槽。

items.en: Old French rifler means to scratch or plunder.
items.cn: 古法语 rifler 意为抓挠或掠夺。

items.en: Rifle first names a grooved gun barrel.
items.cn: rifle 最初指刻有膛线的枪管。

items.en: The gun takes the name of its rifling.
items.cn: 这种枪以膛线之名得名。

items.en: The verb keeps the sense of searching roughly.
items.cn: 动词义保留了粗暴翻找的含义。

note.en: A rifle is a long gun; a pistol is short. To rifle is to search roughly.
note.cn: rifle 是长枪，pistol 是短枪；rifle 作动词指粗暴翻找。

normalIntro.en: A rifle is named for the grooves cut in its barrel.
normalIntro.cn: rifle 因枪管上刻出的沟槽而得名。

normal.en: A rifle rests against the shoulder.
normal.cn: rifle 抵在肩上。

normal.en: Rifle through means search in a hurry.
normal.cn: rifle through 意为匆忙翻找。

normal.en: A rifle range is a place to practise.
normal.cn: rifle range 是练习射击的地方。

normal.en: Old rifles had deep grooves inside.
normal.cn: 旧式步枪内部有很深的沟槽。

normal.en: Rifle the drawer means dig through it.
normal.cn: rifle the drawer 意为翻遍抽屉。

abstract.en: Picture a spiral groove twisting through metal.
abstract.cn: 想象一条螺旋沟槽贯穿金属。

abstract.en: Imagine hands flying through a pile of papers.
abstract.cn: 想象双手在纸堆里飞快翻动。

abstract.en: Think of a long shadow against a barrack wall.
abstract.cn: 想象营房墙上一条长长的影子。

examples.en: The rifle was locked in the cabinet.
examples.cn: 步枪锁在柜子里。

examples.en: Someone had rifled the desk in the night.
examples.cn: 有人夜里翻遍了书桌。

examples.en: He rifled the bag but found nothing.
examples.cn: 他翻遍了包，却什么也没找到。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「riffle（翻页）＋ 枪」——枪管里刻出一圈圈沟槽，就是步枪。

root: 德语 riffel（沟槽）→ 枪管膛线 → rifle（步枪）；动词义另有古法语 rifler（抓挠、掠夺）的来源。

sensesIntro.en: Rifle means a long shoulder gun, or to search through something quickly and roughly.
sensesIntro.cn: rifle 指抵肩射击的长枪，也可指快速粗暴地翻找。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: spiral grooves inside a barrel.
core.cn: 核心意象：枪管内部螺旋的膛线。

branches.en: The grooved barrel gives the gun its name.
branches.cn: 带膛线的枪管给了这种枪名称。

branches.en: Hurried hands scratch through a drawer.
branches.cn: 匆忙的手在抽屉里抓翻。

branches.en: A rough search can become theft.
branches.cn: 粗暴的翻找可能变成偷窃。

branches.en: The groove image links the gun and the quick search.
branches.cn: 沟槽意象把枪与快速翻找连在一起。

branches.en: Searching and plundering share the same rush.
branches.cn: 翻找与洗劫共享同样的急切。

intro.en: Rifle links a German groove word for the barrel to an old French verb for plunder.
intro.cn: rifle 把德语中表示枪管沟槽的词与古法语中表示掠夺的动词联系起来。

latinIntro.en: The gun sense is Germanic, while the search sense comes through French.
latinIntro.cn: 枪义来自日耳曼语，翻找义则经由法语而来。

items.example: Riffel names the cut in metal.
The ending marks a small groove.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾标记细小的沟槽。
rifle 借用了枪管的名字。
rifleman 由 rifle 与 man 组成。
rifle range 增加了地点含义。

items.example: The phrase uses the verb sense.

definition_zh: 正确的；右边的；权利；正好
definition_en: correct, on the right side, a just claim, or exactly
core_image: 路口亮起绿灯后向右转的人
scene: 她在路口向右转，很快就找到了那家书店。She turned right at the corner and soon found the bookshop.
sceneCN: 这里 right 是「右边」（第 2 个义项：朝向右侧的方向）；句意：她在路口向右转，很快就找到了那家书店。

senses.title: Correct
senses.definition: true or correct
senses.example: You gave the right answer.
senses.exampleCN: 你给出了正确答案。
senses.why: What is straight is also what is true.
senses.whyCN: 笔直的东西也就是正确的东西。

senses.title: The right side
senses.definition: the side opposite the left
senses.example: The bank is on your right.
senses.exampleCN: 银行在你的右边。
senses.why: The strong hand side came to be called right.
senses.whyCN: 有力的那只手所在一侧被称为右边。

senses.title: A just claim
senses.definition: something you are morally or legally allowed to have
senses.definitionCN: 在道德或法律上可以拥有的事物
senses.example: Everyone has the right to speak.
senses.exampleCN: 每个人都有说话的权利。
senses.why: A straight rule protects a just claim.
senses.whyCN: 正直的规则保护正当的诉求。

senses.title: Exactly
senses.definition: exactly or directly
senses.example: The book is right here.
senses.exampleCN: 书就在这儿。
senses.why: A straight line reaches exactly where it aims.
senses.whyCN: 直线正好抵达它指向的地方。

intro.en: Right comes from Old English riht, straight, just or true.
intro.cn: right 源自古英语 riht，意为笔直、公正或真实。

items.en: Riht means straight and just.
items.cn: riht 意为笔直与公正。

items.en: Straight becomes correct and right.
items.cn: 笔直引申为正确与正当。

items.en: The right hand gives the side sense.
items.cn: 右手义给出了方位义。

items.en: Rights become legal claims.
items.cn: rights 成为法律上的权利。

items.en: Right now and right away add exactness.
items.cn: right now 与 right away 增加了确切义。

note.en: Right is correct or the right side; rightly means with good reason.
note.cn: right 指正确或右边，rightly 意为有正当理由地。

normalIntro.en: Right begins as straight, and straight becomes correct.
normalIntro.cn: right 最初表示笔直，笔直引申为正确。

normal.en: The right answer is the correct one.
normal.cn: right answer 就是正确的答案。

normal.en: Your right hand is on the right side.
normal.cn: 你的右手就在右边。

normal.en: A right is a just claim.
normal.cn: right 是一种正当诉求。

normal.en: Right now means at this very moment.
normal.cn: right now 意为就在此刻。

normal.en: Rightly means with good reason.
normal.cn: rightly 意为有正当理由地。

abstract.en: Picture a line drawn perfectly straight.
abstract.cn: 想象一条画得笔直的线。

abstract.en: Imagine a hand raised to claim a fair share.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手举起，要求公平的一份。

abstract.en: Think of an arrow pointing exactly at the dot.
abstract.cn: 想象一支箭正好指向圆点。

examples.en: Is this the right way to the station?
examples.cn: 去车站是走这条路吗？

examples.en: She writes with her right hand.
examples.cn: 她用右手写字。

examples.en: Children have the right to learn.
examples.cn: 儿童有学习的权利。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「right」听起来像「直」——笔直、正确，也指向右手那一边。

root: 古英语 riht（笔直、公正）→ 正确、右边、权利，核心义「笔直不分叉的，因而正当」。

sensesIntro.en: Right means correct, the right-hand side, a just claim, or exactly.
sensesIntro.cn: right 意为正确、右边、权利，或正好。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a straight line with no bend.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条笔直不弯的线。

branches.en: Straightness turns into correctness.
branches.cn: 笔直引申为正确。

branches.en: The right hand gives the side word.
branches.cn: 右手给出了方位词。

branches.en: A just claim is a moral straight line.
branches.cn: 正当诉求是一条道德上的直线。

branches.en: Exactly is the straight line hitting its mark.
branches.cn: 正好就是直线命中目标。

branches.en: Correct and just both come from straightness.
branches.cn: 正确与公正都来自笔直。

intro.en: Right is a native English word from Old English riht.
intro.cn: right 是源自古英语 riht 的英语本族词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin cousin rectus, straight, appears in correct and direct.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语近亲 rectus（笔直）出现在 correct 与 direct 中。

items.exampleCN: 复数形式常指各项权利。
rectus 出现在 correct 中。

latinEntries.example: Rectus is the Latin cousin of right.
latinEntries.exampleCN: rectus 是 right 的拉丁近亲。

definition_en: correctly, or for a good and fair reason
core_image: 举杯庆祝团队成果的成员
scene: 她理所当然地为团队的努力感到自豪。She rightly felt proud of her team's effort.
sceneCN: 这里 rightly 是「理所当然地」（第 2 个义项：有充分正当理由地）；句意：她理所当然地为团队的努力感到自豪。

senses.title: Correctly
senses.definition: in a correct way
senses.example: He rightly guessed the answer.
senses.exampleCN: 他正确地猜出了答案。
senses.why: The adverb keeps the straight, correct sense of right.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词保留了 right 笔直、正确的含义。

senses.title: With good reason
senses.definition: justifiably or fairly
senses.example: She rightly refused the unfair offer.
senses.exampleCN: 她理所当然地拒绝了这个不公平的提议。
senses.why: A straight claim deserves a straight answer.
senses.whyCN: 正当的诉求理应得到正当的回应。

intro.en: Rightly is right plus -ly, carrying the old sense of straight and just.
intro.cn: rightly 是 right 加 -ly，承袭了笔直与公正的旧义。

items.en: Rihtlice means rightly or justly.
items.cn: rihtlice 意为正确地或公正地。

items.en: Right keeps the adjective sense.
items.cn: right 保留了形容词义。

items.en: -ly turns it into an adverb.
items.cn: -ly 把它变成副词。

items.en: Rightly often adds praise or justification.
items.cn: rightly 常带有赞许或正当理由。

items.en: Rightly so becomes a common phrase.
items.cn: rightly so 成为常用短语。

note.en: Rightly means with reason; correctly means without error.
note.cn: rightly 强调有理由，correctly 强调没有错误。

normalIntro.en: Rightly is right turned into an adverb.
normalIntro.cn: rightly 就是 right 变成的副词。

normal.en: Rightly so means it is fair to think so.
normal.cn: rightly so 意为这样想是公平的。

normal.en: Quite rightly means with full reason.
normal.cn: quite rightly 意为完全有理由。

normal.en: Rightly called means named correctly.
normal.cn: rightly called 意为被正确地称呼。

normal.en: Rightly proud means proud for good reason.
normal.cn: rightly proud 意为有理由感到自豪。

normal.en: The -ly ending makes it an adverb.
normal.cn: -ly 结尾使它成为副词。

abstract.en: Picture a judge nodding at a fair claim.
abstract.cn: 想象法官对正当的诉求点头。

abstract.en: Imagine a straight arrow finding the centre.
abstract.cn: 想象一支笔直的箭射中中心。

abstract.en: Think of applause that everyone agrees on.
abstract.cn: 想象全场都认同的掌声。

examples.en: They rightly complained about the noise.
examples.cn: 他们理所当然地抱怨了噪音。

examples.en: The city is rightly famous for its gardens.
examples.cn: 这座城市以花园闻名，实至名归。

examples.en: She rightly pointed out the mistake.
examples.cn: 她正确地指出了这个错误。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「right（对）＋ ly」——以正确而正当的方式，就是理所当然地。

root: right（笔直、公正）＋ -ly（方式副词）→ rightly，核心义「以正确而正当的方式」。

sensesIntro.en: Rightly means correctly, or with a fair and good reason.
sensesIntro.cn: rightly 意为正确地，或有公平正当的理由。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fair claim met with agreement.
core.cn: 核心意象：正当的诉求得到认同。

branches.en: Doing it correctly is the first sense.
branches.cn: 正确地做是第一个义项。

branches.en: Having a good reason is the second sense.
branches.cn: 有正当理由是第二个义项。

branches.en: A correct step and a fair step both follow the straight line.
branches.cn: 正确的举动与公平的举动都沿着直线。

branches.en: Praise is often both correct and deserved.
branches.cn: 赞许往往既正确又应得。

branches.en: Rightly so marks a deserved reaction.
branches.cn: rightly so 标记一种应得的反应。

intro.en: Rightly is right plus the adverb suffix -ly.
intro.cn: rightly 是 right 加副词后缀 -ly。

latinIntro.en: The Latin cousin rectus, straight, also lies behind correct.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语近亲 rectus（笔直）也藏在 correct 背后。

definition_zh: 坚硬的；僵硬的；严格的；死板的
definition_en: stiff and unable to bend, or strict and unwilling to change
core_image: 一根弯不动的旧金属管
scene: 这根旧管子已经变得僵硬，轻轻一弯就裂开了。The old pipe had become rigid and cracked when bent.
sceneCN: 这里 rigid 是「僵硬的」（第 1 个义项：坚硬而无法弯曲）；句意：这根旧管子已经变得僵硬，轻轻一弯就裂开了。

pos.zh: 坚硬的；僵硬的；严格的；死板的

senses.title: Stiff to the touch
senses.definition: hard and not able to bend
senses.example: The frame is made of rigid steel.
senses.exampleCN: 框架由坚硬的钢材制成。
senses.why: Rigid begins as the Latin word for stiff.
senses.whyCN: rigid 最初就是拉丁语中表示僵硬的那个词。

senses.title: Strict and fixed
senses.definition: not allowing change or flexibility
senses.example: The school has rigid rules about phones.
senses.exampleCN: 学校对手机有严格的规定。
senses.why: A rule that cannot bend is rigid.
senses.whyCN: 不能变通的规则就是僵硬的。

senses.title: Frozen with feeling
senses.definition: unable to move because of fear or shock
senses.definitionCN: 因恐惧或震惊而无法动弹
senses.example: He stood rigid at the edge of the cliff.
senses.exampleCN: 他僵立在悬崖边。
senses.why: The body turns stiff when terror takes over.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧占据身心时，身体会变得僵硬。

intro.en: Rigid comes from Latin rigidus, stiff, from rigere, to be stiff.
intro.cn: rigid 源自拉丁语 rigidus（僵硬），来自 rigere（变硬）。

items.en: Rigere means to be stiff.
items.cn: rigere 意为僵硬。

items.en: Rigidus means stiff or unbending.
items.cn: rigidus 意为僵硬、不弯。

items.en: French rigide keeps the physical sense.
items.cn: 法语 rigide 保留了物理含义。

items.en: English rigid adds the sense of strict rules.
items.cn: 英语 rigid 增加了严格规则的含义。

items.en: It also describes a body frozen by fear.
items.cn: 它也形容因恐惧而僵住的身体。

note.en: Rigid is stiff in body or rule; strict is firm about rules only.
note.cn: rigid 可指身体或规则僵硬，strict 只强调规则严格。

normalIntro.en: Rigid is a rod that refuses to bend.
normalIntro.cn: rigid 就是一根拒绝弯曲的杆子。

normal.en: Rigid rules leave no room to bend.
normal.cn: rigid rules 不留变通余地。

normal.en: A rigid frame holds its shape.
normal.cn: rigid frame 保持自身形状。

normal.en: Rigid material does not fold.
normal.cn: rigid material 不会折叠。

normal.en: Rigid with fear means frozen still.
normal.cn: rigid with fear 意为吓得僵住。

normal.en: Rigidity is the noun of rigid.
normal.cn: rigidity 是 rigid 的名词形式。

abstract.en: Picture a steel bar under heavy load.
abstract.cn: 想象一根承重的钢条。

abstract.en: Imagine a soldier standing without a twitch.
abstract.cn: 想象一名士兵一动不动地站着。

abstract.en: Think of a frozen branch snapping in wind.
abstract.cn: 想象冻硬的树枝在风中折断。

examples.en: The tent poles are light but rigid.
examples.cn: 帐篷杆又轻又硬。

examples.en: His rigid attitude made talk difficult.
examples.cn: 他死板的态度让谈话很难进行。

examples.en: She sat rigid with shock.
examples.cn: 她震惊得僵坐在那里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rigid」听起来像「硬紧的」——又硬又紧，弯都弯不动。

root: 拉丁语 rigere（变硬）→ rigidus（僵硬的）→ rigid，核心义「硬得无法弯曲，因而不能变通」。

sensesIntro.en: Rigid means physically stiff, strictly fixed, or frozen by strong feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: rigid 意为物理上僵硬、规则上严格固定，或因强烈情绪而僵住。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rod that will not bend.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根弯不动的杆子。

branches.en: Physical stiffness is the root sense.
branches.cn: 物理僵硬是根本义项。

branches.en: A rule that cannot bend becomes rigid.
branches.cn: 不能变通的规则变得僵死。

branches.en: Fear freezes the body into stiffness.
branches.cn: 恐惧把身体冻得僵硬。

branches.en: Stiff steel and stiff rules share one image.
branches.cn: 坚硬的钢与僵硬的规则共享同一个意象。

branches.en: Metal and muscles both lose their give.
branches.cn: 金属与肌肉都失去了弹性。

intro.en: Rigid comes from the Latin root rig, to be stiff.
intro.cn: rigid 来自拉丁词根 rig（僵硬）。

latinIntro.en: Rigere gives rigidus, and French rigide carries it to English.
latinIntro.cn: rigere 给出 rigidus，法语 rigide 把它带入英语。

items.example: Rig carries the idea of stiffness.

latinEntries.example: Rigidus is the source of rigid.
latinEntries.exampleCN: rigidus 是 rigid 的来源。

definition_zh: 暴乱；骚乱；极其好笑的人或事；参与暴乱
definition_en: a violent public disturbance, or something very funny
core_image: 深夜广场上混乱的人群
scene: 广场上的骚乱直到深夜才慢慢平息。The riot in the square only calmed down late at night.
sceneCN: 这里 riot 是「骚乱」（第 1 个义项：公众场所的暴力混乱）；句意：广场上的骚乱直到深夜才慢慢平息。

pos.zh: 暴乱；骚乱；极好笑的人或事

senses.title: A violent crowd
senses.definition: a violent disturbance by a crowd in public
senses.definitionCN: 人群在公共场所的暴力骚乱
senses.example: The riot broke out after the match.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛结束后爆发了骚乱。
senses.why: A crowd that loses control becomes a riot.
senses.whyCN: 失去控制的人群就成了骚乱。

senses.title: Very funny
senses.definition: a person or thing that is very funny
senses.example: His story was an absolute riot.
senses.exampleCN: 他的故事实在太逗了。
senses.why: Wild laughter feels like a small riot.
senses.whyCN: 狂笑的感觉就像一场小小的骚动。

senses.title: To join a riot
senses.definition: to take part in a violent public disturbance
senses.definitionCN: 参与公众场所的暴力骚乱
senses.example: Crowds rioted outside the old factory.
senses.exampleCN: 人群在旧工厂外暴动。
senses.why: The noun turns into the act itself.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为行为本身。

intro.en: Riot comes from Old French riote, a quarrel or wild behaviour.
intro.cn: riot 源自古法语 riote，意为争吵或放荡行为。

items.en: Riote means a quarrel.
items.cn: riote 意为争吵。

items.en: The word also suggests wild living.
items.cn: 该词也暗示放荡的生活。

items.en: Riot comes to mean public disorder.
items.cn: riot 逐渐指公众骚乱。

items.en: Riot police appear to control crowds.
items.cn: 防暴警察出现以控制人群。

items.en: A riot can also mean great fun.
items.cn: a riot 也可以指极大的乐趣。

note.en: A riot is violent; a protest may be peaceful.
note.cn: riot 是暴力的，protest 可能是和平的。

entries.definition: an act that breaks the peace

normalIntro.en: A riot is a crowd that has lost its brakes.
normalIntro.cn: riot 就是失去刹车的人群。

normal.en: Riot police deal with violent crowds.
normal.cn: riot police 应对暴力人群。

normal.en: To start a riot is to cause disorder.
normal.cn: start a riot 就是引发混乱。

normal.en: Run riot means act without control.
normal.cn: run riot 意为失控妄为。

normal.en: A riot of colour means many bright colours.
normal.cn: a riot of colour 意为五彩缤纷。

normal.en: If a show is a riot, it is very funny.
normal.cn: 如果演出是 a riot，就说明它非常逗。

abstract.en: Picture a street full of shouting shadows.
abstract.cn: 想象满是呼喊人影的街道。

abstract.en: Imagine laughter breaking out like a small storm.
abstract.cn: 想象笑声像小风暴一样爆发。

abstract.en: Think of a garden bursting with wild colour.
abstract.cn: 想象花园里色彩狂放。

examples.en: The riot lasted until dawn.
examples.cn: 骚乱持续到黎明。

examples.en: The party was a riot from start to finish.
examples.cn: 这场聚会从头到尾都非常欢乐。

examples.en: The crowd rioted after the decision.
examples.cn: 裁决之后人群发生了暴动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「riot」听起来像「乱特」——特别乱的场面，就是骚乱。

root: 古法语 riote（争吵、放荡）→ 公众骚乱 → 动词「参与暴乱」，核心义「失控的喧嚣」。

sensesIntro.en: A riot is a violent public disturbance, a very funny thing, or the act of rioting.
sensesIntro.cn: riot 指暴力骚乱、极好笑的事物，或参与暴乱的行为。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crowd with no brakes.
core.cn: 核心意象：失去刹车的人群。

branches.en: A violent crowd is the public sense.
branches.cn: 暴力人群是公众义。

branches.en: Uncontrolled laughter borrows the wild image.
branches.cn: 失控的笑借用了狂放的意象。

branches.en: The verb names joining the disorder.
branches.cn: 动词义指加入混乱。

branches.en: The noun and verb both point at the same streets.
branches.cn: 名词与动词都指向同样的街头。

branches.en: Violence and wild fun both mean losing control.
branches.cn: 暴力与狂乐都意味着失去控制。

intro.en: Riot is a French borrowing with no living prefix.
intro.cn: riot 是法语借词，没有仍在使用的词缀。

latinIntro.en: French riote is its direct parent.
latinIntro.cn: 法语 riote 是它的直接来源。

items.exampleCN: riot 去掉了词尾的 e。
这个复合词指一支警力。

items.example: Run riot uses the wild idea.
items.exampleCN: run riot 使用了狂放的意象。

definition_en: to tear something quickly, or a torn place
core_image: 被撕成两半的信封
scene: 她不小心把信封撕成了两半。She accidentally ripped the envelope in half.
sceneCN: 这里 rip 是「撕」（第 1 个义项：用力快速把东西扯开）；句意：她不小心把信封撕成了两半。

senses.title: Tearing quickly
senses.definition: to tear something with force
senses.example: He ripped the letter into small pieces.
senses.exampleCN: 他把信撕成了小片。
senses.why: Rip suggests a fast, rough pull.
senses.whyCN: rip 意味着一记快速粗暴的拉扯。

senses.title: Charging too much
senses.definition: to charge an unfair price
senses.example: That shop rips off tourists.
senses.exampleCN: 那家店宰游客。
senses.why: Ripping away money feels like tearing cloth.
senses.whyCN: 把钱撕走就像撕布一样。

senses.title: A torn place
senses.definition: a hole or tear in something
senses.example: There is a rip in my coat.
senses.exampleCN: 我的外套上有个裂口。
senses.why: The noun keeps the shape of the tear.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了撕裂的形状。

intro.en: Rip is a Middle English word, probably from a Scandinavian source, meaning to tear.
intro.cn: rip 是中古英语词，可能来自斯堪的纳维亚语，意为撕开。

items.en: Rippen means to tear.
items.cn: rippen 意为撕。

items.en: A related northern word also means to tear.
items.cn: 北欧的相关词同样意为撕。

items.en: Rip becomes common for cloth and paper.
items.cn: rip 常用于布料和纸张。

items.en: Rip off grows into a slang phrase.
items.cn: rip off 发展为俚语短语。

items.en: The noun names a tear in fabric.
items.cn: 名词指织物上的撕口。

note.en: Rip is a fast, rough tear; tear itself is the general word.
note.cn: rip 是快速粗暴的撕，tear 是一般的撕裂。

entries.definition: to make a long narrow cut

normalIntro.en: Rip is the sound and speed of a tear.
normalIntro.cn: rip 就是撕裂的声音与速度。

normal.en: Rip open means tear it at once.
normal.cn: rip open 意为立刻撕开。

normal.en: Rip apart means tear it into pieces.
normal.cn: rip apart 意为撕成碎片。

normal.en: Rip off means charge far too much.
normal.cn: rip off 意为要价过高。

normal.en: A rip in the paper is a torn place.
normal.cn: a rip in the paper 是一处撕口。

normal.en: Ripped jeans are torn on purpose.
normal.cn: ripped jeans 是故意撕破的牛仔裤。

abstract.en: Picture cloth parting with a sharp sound.
abstract.cn: 想象布料伴着锐响裂开。

abstract.en: Imagine a page pulled in two by quick hands.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手飞快地把纸页扯成两半。

abstract.en: Think of a lightning tear across the sky.
abstract.cn: 想象闪电在天空撕开一道口子。

examples.en: The dog ripped my new shirt.
examples.cn: 狗撕破了我新买的衬衫。

examples.en: Do not rip off the label yet.
examples.cn: 先别把标签撕掉。

examples.en: There was a long rip in the tent.
examples.cn: 帐篷上有一道长长的裂口。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rip」听起来像「裂扑」——一下裂开扑啦响，就是撕。

root: 中古英语 rippen（撕）→ rip，核心义「快速粗暴地扯开」；俚语义「敲竹杠」像把钱撕走。

sensesIntro.en: Rip means to tear something quickly, to overcharge, or a torn place.
sensesIntro.cn: rip 意为快速撕开、敲竹杠，或指一处裂口。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: cloth parting with a sharp sound.
core.cn: 核心意象：布料伴着锐响裂开。

branches.en: The fast pull is the core action.
branches.cn: 快速拉扯是核心动作。

branches.en: Pulling away money becomes overcharging.
branches.cn: 把钱拉走引申为敲竹杠。

branches.en: The noun keeps the shape of the tear.
branches.cn: 名词保留了撕口的形状。

branches.en: The action and its result share one image.
branches.cn: 动作与结果共享同一个意象。

branches.en: Both cloth and wallets can be ripped.
branches.cn: 布料与钱包都可能被「撕」。

intro.en: Rip is a short native verb with no prefix.
intro.cn: rip 是简短的本族动词，没有前缀。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic rather than Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属于日耳曼语而非拉丁语。

items.exampleCN: 破洞牛仔裤是一种风格。

items.example: The phrase adds a slang sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语增加了俚语义。
这个短语体现快速动作。

definition_zh: 成熟的；时机成熟的；年纪大的
definition_en: ready to eat or ready to happen
core_image: 枝头熟透的桃子
scene: 果园里的桃子已经成熟，等着人来摘。The peaches in the orchard were ripe and ready to pick.
sceneCN: 这里 ripe 是「成熟的」（第 1 个义项：果实可以食用）；句意：果园里的桃子已经成熟，等着人来摘。

pos.zh: 成熟的；时机成熟的；年高的

senses.title: Ready to eat
senses.definition: fully grown and ready to eat
senses.example: These apples are not ripe yet.
senses.exampleCN: 这些苹果还没熟。
senses.why: Fruit is ripe when it has reached its full season.
senses.whyCN: 果实到了季节的顶点就是熟了。

senses.title: Ready to happen
senses.definition: fully prepared for something to happen
senses.definitionCN: 为某事的发生做好充分准备
senses.example: The country was ripe for change.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家变革的时机已成熟。
senses.why: A ready time is like fruit ready to fall.
senses.whyCN: 时机成熟就像果实准备落地。

senses.title: Advanced in years
senses.definition: old and full of experience
senses.example: She lived to a ripe old age.
senses.exampleCN: 她活到了高龄。
senses.why: A long life is also a kind of ripening.
senses.whyCN: 漫长的一生也是一种成熟。

intro.en: Ripe comes from Old English rīpe, ready for harvest.
intro.cn: ripe 源自古英语 rīpe，意为可以收获的。

items.en: Ripe means ready for harvest.
items.cn: ripe 意为可以收获。

items.en: The word spreads from fruit to plans.
items.cn: 这个词从果实扩展到计划。

items.en: Ripe for change means ready for it.
items.cn: ripe for change 意为准备好改变。

items.en: Ripe old age praises long life.
items.cn: ripe old age 赞颂长寿。

items.en: Ripen grows as the verb.
items.cn: ripen 成为对应的动词。

note.en: Ripe fruit is ready to eat; mature is the more general word.
note.cn: ripe 指果实可食，mature 是更一般的「成熟」。

normalIntro.en: Ripe means the fruit has reached its moment.
normalIntro.cn: ripe 意为果实到了它最好的时刻。

normal.en: Ripe fruit falls easily from the branch.
normal.cn: ripe fruit 很容易从枝头落下。

normal.en: Ripe bananas are soft and sweet.
normal.cn: ripe bananas 又软又甜。

normal.en: The time is ripe means now is the moment.
normal.cn: the time is ripe 意为现在正是时候。

normal.en: Ripe for change means ready for it.
normal.cn: ripe for change 意为准备好改变。

normal.en: Ripen is the verb that makes fruit ripe.
normal.cn: ripen 是让果实变熟的动词。

abstract.en: Picture a peach glowing in late summer light.
abstract.cn: 想象夏末阳光下发亮的桃子。

abstract.en: Imagine a bell ready to ring.
abstract.cn: 想象一口随时会响的钟。

abstract.en: Think of a long life full like a harvest.
abstract.cn: 想象一段像丰收般充实的长寿。

examples.en: The melon is sweet and ripe.
examples.cn: 这瓜又甜又熟。

examples.en: Conditions were ripe for a new start.
examples.cn: 重新开始的条件已经成熟。

examples.en: He died at a ripe old age.
examples.cn: 他在高龄时去世。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ripe」听起来像「来盼」——果实盼到最好的时候，就是成熟。

root: 古英语 rīpe（可收获的）→ 成熟 → 时机成熟、年高，核心义「到了可以收获的时刻」。

sensesIntro.en: Ripe means ready to eat, ready to happen, or advanced in age.
sensesIntro.cn: ripe 意为可以食用、时机成熟，或年事已高。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a peach glowing in late summer.
core.cn: 核心意象：夏末发亮的桃子。

branches.en: Fruit ready to eat is the first sense.
branches.cn: 可以食用的果实是第一个义项。

branches.en: A ready moment borrows the fruit image.
branches.cn: 成熟的时机借用了果实的意象。

branches.en: A long life is a final ripening.
branches.cn: 漫长的一生是最后的成熟。

branches.en: Fruit and plans both wait for their moment.
branches.cn: 果实与计划都在等待自己的时刻。

branches.en: Good timing and long life both mean fullness.
branches.cn: 好时机与长寿都意味着圆满。

intro.en: Ripe is a native English adjective from Old English rīpe.
intro.cn: ripe 是源自古英语 rīpe 的英语本族形容词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin prefix; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁前缀，该词属于日耳曼语。

items.exampleCN: ripe 保留了收获的含义。

definition_en: to move upward, stand up, or increase; also the act of rising
core_image: 海面上缓缓升起的太阳
scene: 太阳从海面上升起，渔船陆续出海。The sun rose over the sea and the boats set out.
sceneCN: 这里 rise 是「升起」（第 1 个义项：向上移动）；句意：太阳从海面上升起，渔船陆续出海。

senses.title: Moving upward
senses.definition: to move from a lower place to a higher one
senses.example: Smoke rose from the chimney.
senses.exampleCN: 烟从烟囱里升起。
senses.why: The core act is simple upward movement.
senses.whyCN: 核心动作就是单纯的向上移动。

senses.title: Standing up
senses.definition: to get up from sitting or lying
senses.example: Everyone rose when the judge entered.
senses.exampleCN: 法官进来时大家都站了起来。
senses.why: Standing lifts the body upward.
senses.whyCN: 站立就是把身体向上抬起。

senses.title: An increase
senses.definition: an increase in amount or level
senses.example: There was a sharp rise in prices.
senses.exampleCN: 物价急剧上涨。
senses.why: A number that goes up is also rising.
senses.whyCN: 数字向上走也是上升。

senses.title: A beginning
senses.definition: the start or cause of something
senses.example: The quarrel gave rise to a long feud.
senses.exampleCN: 这场争吵引发了长期的仇怨。
senses.why: Things rise from a source, as smoke from fire.
senses.whyCN: 事物从源头升起，就像烟从火起。

intro.en: Rise comes from Old English rīsan, to rise or get up.
intro.cn: rise 源自古英语 rīsan，意为升起或起身。

items.en: Rīsan means to rise.
items.cn: rīsan 意为升起。

items.en: The sun and smoke both rise.
items.cn: 太阳与烟都会升起。

items.en: Prices begin to rise in trade talk.
items.cn: 贸易语境中价格开始上涨。

items.en: Give rise to means cause.
items.cn: give rise to 意为引起。

items.en: Rise stays irregular: rise, rose, risen.
items.cn: rise 保持不规则变化：rise、rose、risen。

note.en: Rise does not take an object; raise needs one.
note.cn: rise 不带宾语，raise 需要带宾语。

normalIntro.en: Rise is the upward line of smoke or sun.
normalIntro.cn: rise 就是烟或太阳向上的那条线。

normal.en: The sun rises in the east.
normal.cn: the sun rises 太阳从东方升起。

normal.en: Rise up means get up or fight back.
normal.cn: rise up 意为起身或反抗。

normal.en: A sharp rise means a fast increase.
normal.cn: a sharp rise 意为快速上涨。

normal.en: Give rise to means cause something.
normal.cn: give rise to 意为引起某事。

normal.en: Rise above means go beyond a problem.
normal.cn: rise above 意为超越问题。

abstract.en: Picture a red sun lifting off the water.
abstract.cn: 想象一轮红日从水面升起。

abstract.en: Imagine smoke curling up a cold chimney.
abstract.cn: 想象烟从冰冷的烟囱里卷上去。

abstract.en: Think of a graph line climbing to the right.
abstract.cn: 想象一条折线向右上方攀升。

examples.en: Prices rose by ten percent last year.
examples.cn: 去年物价上涨了百分之十。

examples.en: She rose to answer the question.
examples.cn: 她站起来回答问题。

examples.en: The plan gave rise to many doubts.
examples.cn: 这个计划引起了诸多疑虑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rise」听起来像「拉起」——被拉起来，就是上升。

root: 古英语 rīsan（升起）→ rise，核心义「自下而上移动」，从太阳、身体到物价与起因都能延伸。

sensesIntro.en: Rise means to go up, to stand, to increase, or to begin from a source.
sensesIntro.cn: rise 意为向上、起身、增长，或从某处起源。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an upward line against the sky.
core.cn: 核心意象：天空下一条向上的线。

branches.en: Simple upward movement is the core.
branches.cn: 单纯的向上移动是核心。

branches.en: Standing raises the body from a chair.
branches.cn: 站起是把身体从椅子上抬起。

branches.en: Numbers that grow follow the same line.
branches.cn: 增长的数字沿着同样的线。

branches.en: A source sends things upward like smoke.
branches.cn: 源头把事物像烟一样向上送出。

branches.en: Physical and numeric rising share one image.
branches.cn: 物理上升与数字上涨共享同一个意象。

intro.en: Rise is a native irregular verb from Old English rīsan.
intro.cn: rise 是源自古英语 rīsan 的英语本族不规则动词。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic; ar- in arise is its closest prefix.
latinIntro.cn: 该词属于日耳曼语，arise 中的 ar- 是它最接近的前缀。

items.exampleCN: arise 是 rise 加 a-。

definition_en: the chance that something bad will happen, or to put something in danger
core_image: 不顾坏天气出发的登山者
scene: 登山者不顾天气变坏，冒着被困山中的风险出发。The climbers set off despite the weather, risking being trapped.
sceneCN: 这里 risk 是「冒…的风险」（第 3 个义项：把某事置于危险之中）；句意：登山者不顾天气变坏，冒着被困山中的风险出发。

senses.title: Chance of harm
senses.definition: the possibility that something bad will happen
senses.example: There is a risk of heavy rain tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 今晚有大雨的风险。
senses.why: The noun names the chance of loss before it comes.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指损失尚未发生前的可能性。

senses.title: A dangerous person or thing
senses.definition: someone or something likely to cause harm
senses.definitionCN: 可能造成伤害的人或事物
senses.example: That old bridge is a risk to traffic.
senses.exampleCN: 那座旧桥对交通是个隐患。
senses.why: A risk can be the source, not only the chance.
senses.whyCN: 风险也可以指源头，而不只是可能性。

senses.title: To put in danger
senses.definition: to do something that may cause loss or harm
senses.definitionCN: 做可能带来损失或伤害的事
senses.example: He risked his job to help her.
senses.exampleCN: 他冒着丢掉工作的风险去帮她。
senses.why: The verb makes the chance personal and active.
senses.whyCN: 动词让这种可能性变得个人化且主动。

intro.en: Risk comes from French risque, probably from Italian risco, danger.
intro.cn: risk 源自法语 risque，可能来自意大利语 risco（危险）。

items.en: Risco means danger or bold chance.
items.cn: risco 意为危险或大胆的冒险。

items.en: Risque carries the word into French.
items.cn: risque 把词带入法语。

items.en: Risk enters English as a noun of chance.
items.cn: risk 以表示可能性的名词进入英语。

items.en: Insurance and health give it new uses.
items.cn: 保险与健康领域赋予它新用法。

items.en: The verb risk grows beside the noun.
items.cn: 动词 risk 与名词并行发展。

note.en: A risk is a chance of loss; a danger is the harm itself.
note.cn: risk 是损失的几率，danger 是伤害本身。

normalIntro.en: Risk is the shadow of a bad outcome.
normalIntro.cn: risk 是坏结果的影子。

normal.en: At risk means in danger.
normal.cn: at risk 意为处于危险中。

normal.en: Take a risk means accept a chance of loss.
normal.cn: take a risk 意为接受损失的可能。

normal.en: A health risk may hurt your body.
normal.cn: health risk 可能伤害身体。

normal.en: Risk of failure is the chance of failing.
normal.cn: risk of failure 是失败的可能。

normal.en: To risk your life is to put it in danger.
normal.cn: risk your life 就是把生命置于危险中。

abstract.en: Picture a thin bridge over a deep valley.
abstract.cn: 想象一座横跨深谷的细桥。

abstract.en: Imagine stepping onto thin ice in spring.
abstract.cn: 想象春天踩上薄冰。

abstract.en: Think of a coin thrown into the dark.
abstract.cn: 想象把一枚硬币扔进黑暗。

examples.en: Smoking increases the risk of illness.
examples.cn: 吸烟会增加患病的风险。

examples.en: They risked everything for the farm.
examples.cn: 他们为农场冒了一切风险。

examples.en: The children are at risk near the river.
examples.cn: 孩子们在河边很危险。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「risk」听起来像「锐思刻」——反复思量那一刻的危险，就是风险。

root: 意大利语 risco（危险）→ 法语 risque → risk，核心义「坏事发生前的可能，以及主动迎向它的行动」。

sensesIntro.en: Risk means the chance of harm, a source of harm, or to put something in danger.
sensesIntro.cn: risk 意为受害的可能、危险的源头，或使某物陷入危险。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin bridge over a deep drop.
core.cn: 核心意象：深谷上的一座细桥。

branches.en: The chance of loss is the main sense.
branches.cn: 损失的可能性是主要义项。

branches.en: A dangerous thing is a risk in itself.
branches.cn: 危险的事物本身就是风险。

branches.en: The verb makes someone face the chance.
branches.cn: 动词让人主动面对这种可能。

branches.en: Chance and source both wear the same word.
branches.cn: 可能与源头共用同一个词。

branches.en: To risk is to accept the chance of loss.
branches.cn: 冒险就是接受损失的可能。

intro.en: Risk is a Romance borrowing, from Italian and French.
intro.cn: risk 是来自意大利语与法语的罗曼语借词。

latinIntro.en: Italian risco is the earliest known form.
latinIntro.cn: 意大利语 risco 是目前已知的最早形式。

items.example: Risque carries the word to French.

definition_zh: 对手；竞争者；与…匹敌；竞争的
definition_en: a person or group competing for the same thing, or to match them
core_image: 同一条街上争抢客人的两家小店
scene: 同一条街上的两家店铺互相竞争，争抢同一批客人。The two shops on the same street are rivals for the same customers.
sceneCN: 这里 rival 是「对手」（第 1 个义项：争夺同一目标的竞争者）；句意：同一条街上的两家店铺互相竞争，争抢同一批客人。

senses.title: One who competes
senses.definition: a person or group trying to win the same thing
senses.definitionCN: 试图赢得同一目标的人或群体
senses.example: Her main rival trains in the same gym.
senses.exampleCN: 她的主要对手在同一家健身房训练。
senses.why: Two people sharing one stream must compete for it.
senses.whyCN: 共用一条溪流的人必然要争夺它。

senses.title: To match someone
senses.definition: to be as good as someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 与某人或某物一样出色
senses.example: No one can rival her skill at chess.
senses.exampleCN: 没人能在棋艺上与她匹敌。
senses.why: A worthy opponent raises the level of both.
senses.whyCN: 强劲的对手会把双方的水平都抬高。

senses.title: Competing
senses.definition: competing for the same market or aim
senses.definitionCN: 争夺同一市场或目标的
senses.example: The rival firm cut its prices.
senses.exampleCN: 竞争对手公司降低了价格。
senses.why: The adjective marks the other side of the race.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标记竞赛的另一方。

intro.en: Rival comes from Latin rivalis, one who uses the same stream, from rivus, a stream.
intro.cn: rival 源自拉丁语 rivalis，意为共用同一条溪流的人，来自 rivus（溪流）。

items.en: Rivus means a stream.
items.cn: rivus 意为溪流。

items.en: Rivalis is one who shares the stream.
items.cn: rivalis 指共用溪流的人。

items.en: French rival keeps the sense of a competitor.
items.cn: 法语 rival 保留了竞争者的含义。

items.en: English rival names a rival in love or sport.
items.cn: 英语 rival 指情感或竞技中的对手。

items.en: Business gives the word its widest use.
items.cn: 商业让这个词使用最广。

note.en: A rival is close enough to compete; an enemy wishes to harm.
note.cn: rival 是实力相当、彼此竞争的对手，enemy 是想伤害对方的人。

entries.definition: the other side in a contest

normalIntro.en: Rivals once shared one stream and fought over it.
normalIntro.cn: rival 原本指共用一条溪流并为之争夺的人。

normal.en: A rival company wants your customers.
normal.cn: rival company 想要你的顾客。

normal.en: A business rival is a firm you compete with.
normal.cn: business rival 是与你在生意上竞争的公司。

normal.en: A rival team stands on the other side.
normal.cn: rival team 站在赛场的另一边。

normal.en: An arch rival is your biggest opponent.
normal.cn: arch rival 是你最大的对手。

normal.en: Rivalry is the noun for the fight between them.
normal.cn: rivalry 是双方对抗的名词。

abstract.en: Picture two farmers at one narrow ditch.
abstract.cn: 想象两个农夫在一条窄渠两端。

abstract.en: Imagine two runners shoulder to shoulder.
abstract.cn: 想象两名跑者肩并着肩。

abstract.en: Think of two shop signs facing each other.
abstract.cn: 想象两块店招面对面挂起。

examples.en: The two cities are rivals for the trade.
examples.cn: 这两座城市是贸易上的竞争对手。

examples.en: Nobody could rival his patience.
examples.cn: 没有人能比得上他的耐心。

examples.en: A rival seller opened next door.
examples.cn: 一位竞争卖家在隔壁开了店。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rival」听起来像「来否」——总来争抢同一个目标的，就是对手。

root: 拉丁语 rivus（溪流）→ rivalis（共用溪流者）→ rival，核心义「争夺同一资源、实力相当的对手」。

sensesIntro.en: A rival competes for the same goal, can match another's ability, or acts as a competing force.
sensesIntro.cn: rival 指争夺同一目标的对手，也可指与某人匹敌，或作形容词表示竞争的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people at one narrow stream.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个人在一条窄溪旁。

branches.en: The competitor is the main noun sense.
branches.cn: 竞争者是最主要的名词义项。

branches.en: To match a rival is to reach their level.
branches.cn: 与对手匹敌就是达到他们的水平。

branches.en: The adjective marks the opposite side.
branches.cn: 形容词标记对立的一方。

branches.en: Real rivals make each other stronger.
branches.cn: 真正的对手让彼此更强。

branches.en: The noun and adjective both name the other side.
branches.cn: 名词与形容词都指另一方。

intro.en: Rival comes from Latin rivus, a stream.
intro.cn: rival 来自拉丁语 rivus（溪流）。

latinIntro.en: Rivalis, one who shares a stream, gives the French and English word.
latinIntro.cn: rivalis（共用溪流的人）给出了法语和英语中的这个词。

latinEntries.example: Rivus explains why rivals share water.
latinEntries.exampleCN: rivus 解释了对手为何共享水源。

latinEntries.example: Rivalis is the source of rival.
latinEntries.exampleCN: rivalis 是 rival 的来源。

definition_en: a large natural stream of water, or a large flowing mass
core_image: 顺流漂向远方村庄的小船
scene: 小船顺着河流漂向远处的村庄。The boat drifted down the river toward the far village.
sceneCN: 这里 river 是「河流」（第 1 个义项：天然的大水道）；句意：小船顺着河流漂向远处的村庄。

senses.title: A watercourse
senses.definition: a large natural stream flowing to the sea or a lake
senses.definitionCN: 流向海洋或湖泊的大型天然水道
senses.example: The river flows through three countries.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河流经三个国家。
senses.why: The river is the moving water itself.
senses.whyCN: river 指流动的水本身。

senses.title: A great flow
senses.definition: a large moving mass of people or things
senses.example: A river of people filled the square.
senses.exampleCN: 人潮如河般填满了广场。
senses.why: Anything flowing in a long line looks like a river.
senses.whyCN: 任何排成长线流动的东西都像一条河。

senses.title: A source of life
senses.definition: the waterway that supports farms, towns and travel
senses.definitionCN: 供养农田、城镇与交通的水道
senses.example: The town grew rich beside the river.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城镇在河边富了起来。
senses.why: Rivers carry water, soil and trade.
senses.whyCN: 河流带来水、泥土与贸易。

intro.en: River comes from Old French riviere, from Latin riparius, of a bank.
intro.cn: river 源自古法语 riviere，来自拉丁语 riparius（河岸的）。

items.en: Ripa means a bank of a stream.
items.cn: ripa 意为溪流的岸。

items.en: Riparius means of a bank.
items.cn: riparius 意为河岸的。

items.en: Riviere shifts from bank to the water itself.
items.cn: riviere 从河岸转为指水本身。

items.en: River enters English as a large stream.
items.cn: river 以大型水道之意进入英语。

items.en: Figurative rivers of people appear.
items.cn: 出现了人潮如河的比喻用法。

note.en: A river is large; a stream or brook is smaller.
note.cn: river 较大，stream 与 brook 较小。

entries.definition: a river or canal used for travel

normalIntro.en: A river is a road made of flowing water.
normalIntro.cn: river 是一条用水流铺成的路。

normal.en: The river bank is the land beside it.
normal.cn: river bank 是河边的陆地。

normal.en: Cross the river means reach the other side.
normal.cn: cross the river 意为到达对岸。

normal.en: Walk along the river for a calm view.
normal.cn: 沿河散步可看到平静的景色。

normal.en: River water is fresh, not salty.
normal.cn: river water 是淡水，不是咸水。

normal.en: An underground river hides below the land.
normal.cn: underground river 藏在地下。

abstract.en: Picture a silver ribbon between green fields.
abstract.cn: 想象绿色田野间一条银色丝带。

abstract.en: Imagine a crowd flowing like water down a street.
abstract.cn: 想象人群像水一样沿街流动。

abstract.en: Think of an old town waking beside the water.
abstract.cn: 想象一座老城在水边苏醒。

examples.en: We swam in the river all afternoon.
examples.cn: 我们整个下午都在河里游泳。

examples.en: The river was too wide to cross.
examples.cn: 河水太宽，过不去。

examples.en: A river of light ran down the hill.
examples.cn: 一道光河沿山坡流下。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「river」听起来像「日我」——每天都流过我身边的水，就是河流。

root: 拉丁语 ripa（河岸）→ riparius（河岸的）→ 古法语 riviere → river，词义由「岸」转指流动的水道。

sensesIntro.en: A river is a large natural waterway, a great flow of people or things, or a lifeline for a place.
sensesIntro.cn: river 指大型天然水道、大量流动的人或物，以及一个地方的生命依托。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a silver ribbon between fields.
core.cn: 核心意象：田野间的银色丝带。

branches.en: The watercourse is the core sense.
branches.cn: 水道是核心义项。

branches.en: Any great flow borrows the image.
branches.cn: 任何大量流动都借用这个意象。

branches.en: Water, soil and trade make a lifeline.
branches.cn: 水、泥土与贸易构成生命线。

branches.en: Water and people both move in long lines.
branches.cn: 水与人都以长线流动。

branches.en: The stream that feeds a town is also its road.
branches.cn: 供养城镇的河流也是它的道路。

intro.en: River descends from Latin ripa, a bank, through French.
intro.cn: river 经由法语源自拉丁语 ripa（河岸）。

latinIntro.en: Ripa and riparius are the Latin steps behind the word.
latinIntro.cn: ripa 与 riparius 是这个词背后的拉丁环节。

items.example: Riviere shifts to the water itself.

items.exampleCN: riverbed 由 river 与 bed 组成。

latinEntries.example: Ripa is the root of river.
latinEntries.exampleCN: ripa 是 river 的词根。

definition_en: a hard way for vehicles, or a route toward a goal
core_image: 雨后泥泞的乡间小路
scene: 雨后乡间的小路泥泞难走，他们放慢了车速。After the rain the country road was muddy, so they drove slowly.
sceneCN: 这里 road 是「道路」（第 1 个义项：供车辆通行的路面）；句意：雨后乡间的小路泥泞难走，他们放慢了车速。

senses.title: A way for vehicles
senses.definition: a hard surface built for cars and other vehicles
senses.definitionCN: 为汽车等车辆修建的坚硬路面
senses.example: The road is closed for repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 这条路因维修封闭。
senses.why: The road is the prepared line of travel.
senses.whyCN: 道路是修整好的通行线路。

senses.title: A journey
senses.definition: travel or a journey along a route
senses.example: The band has been on the road for months.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队已经巡演了好几个月。
senses.why: Being on the road means being in motion.
senses.whyCN: on the road 意为一直在路上。

senses.title: A way to a goal
senses.definition: a course of action leading to a result
senses.example: Education is the road to a better life.
senses.exampleCN: 教育是通往更好生活的道路。
senses.why: A goal is reached by following a route.
senses.whyCN: 目标要沿着一条路线才能抵达。

intro.en: Road comes from Old English rād, a riding or journey, from ridan, to ride.
intro.cn: road 源自古英语 rād（骑行、旅程），来自 ridan（骑）。

items.en: Rād means a riding or journey.
items.cn: rād 意为骑行或旅程。

items.en: Road shifts from journey to the way itself.
items.cn: road 由旅程转指道路本身。

items.en: Turnpikes make roads common objects.
items.cn: 收费公路让道路成为常见事物。

items.en: On the road means travelling.
items.cn: on the road 意为在路上旅行。

items.en: Road maps guide both cars and plans.
items.cn: 路线图既指引车辆也指引计划。

note.en: A road is for vehicles; a street usually has buildings beside it.
note.cn: road 供车辆通行，street 通常两侧有建筑。

entries.definition: a road in a town with buildings
the way from one place to another

normalIntro.en: A road began as the act of riding.
normalIntro.cn: road 最初指的是骑行的行为。

normal.en: The main road carries most traffic.
normal.cn: main road 承载大部分车流。

normal.en: Road safety saves lives.
normal.cn: road safety 能拯救生命。

normal.en: On the road means travelling.
normal.cn: on the road 意为在旅途中。

normal.en: A road map shows the way.
normal.cn: road map 显示路线。

normal.en: Cross the road at the lights.
normal.cn: cross the road 要在红绿灯处过。

abstract.en: Picture a wet lane shining after rain.
abstract.cn: 想象雨后发亮的湿漉小路。

abstract.en: Imagine a band's van rolling from town to town.
abstract.cn: 想象乐队的车从小镇开往小镇。

abstract.en: Think of a long straight line toward a bright gate.
abstract.cn: 想象一条通向明亮大门的长直线。

examples.en: The road to the village is very narrow.
examples.cn: 通往村庄的路非常窄。

examples.en: They are on the road again this week.
examples.cn: 他们这周又上路了。

examples.en: Hard work is the road to success.
examples.cn: 努力是通往成功的道路。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「road」听起来像「绕的」——弯来绕去让人走的，就是道路。

root: 古英语 rād（骑行、旅程）→ 行走的路线 → road，核心义「被踩出来、供人前往的路线」。

sensesIntro.en: A road is a way for vehicles, the state of travelling, or a route to a goal.
sensesIntro.cn: road 指车辆通行的道路、在旅途中的状态，或通往目标的途径。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wet lane shining after rain.
core.cn: 核心意象：雨后发亮的小路。

branches.en: The built way for vehicles is the main sense.
branches.cn: 为车辆修建的路是主要义项。

branches.en: Being on the road is being in motion.
branches.cn: on the road 就是处于行进中。

branches.en: A plan also follows a road to its result.
branches.cn: 计划也沿着一条路抵达结果。

branches.en: The physical way and the journey share one line.
branches.cn: 实体的路与旅程共享同一条线。

branches.en: Travelling and striving both mean moving toward something.
branches.cn: 旅行与奋斗都意味着朝某处前进。

intro.en: Road comes from Old English rād, riding or journey.
intro.cn: road 源自古英语 rād（骑行、旅程）。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic and shares a root with ride.
latinIntro.cn: 该词属于日耳曼语，与 ride 同源。

items.example: Road shifted to the way itself.

items.exampleCN: roadblock 由 road 与 block 组成。

items.meaning: map of roads or a plan
items.exampleCN: road map 延伸到计划含义。

definition_en: to make a loud deep sound, or such a sound itself
core_image: 夜色中昂首长吼的狮子
scene: 狮子在夜色中发出一声长吼，声音传得很远。The lion's roar carried far into the night.
sceneCN: 这里 roar 是「吼声」（第 1 个义项：动物发出的低沉巨响）；句意：狮子在夜色中发出一声长吼，声音传得很远。

senses.title: An animal's deep cry
senses.definition: a long loud sound made by a large animal
senses.definitionCN: 大型动物发出的长而响的声音
senses.example: We heard a lion roar across the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 我们听见狮子在山谷对面吼叫。
senses.why: The deep open sound belongs first to big animals.
senses.whyCN: 这种深沉开阔的声音首先属于大型动物。

senses.title: A human shout
senses.definition: to shout in a very loud voice
senses.example: He roared at the driver to stop.
senses.exampleCN: 他朝司机大吼让车停下。
senses.why: Anger or excitement makes the voice animal-loud.
senses.whyCN: 愤怒或激动会让人的声音大得像野兽。

senses.title: A loud engine sound
senses.definition: a loud continuous noise, as of engines or traffic
senses.definitionCN: 发动机或车流等发出的持续巨响
senses.example: The roar of the truck shook the windows.
senses.exampleCN: 卡车的轰鸣震动了窗户。
senses.why: Machines can sound like a beast in the dark.
senses.whyCN: 机器在黑暗中听起来像一头野兽。

intro.en: Roar comes from Old English rārian, to roar like a beast.
intro.cn: roar 源自古英语 rārian，意为像野兽般吼叫。

items.en: Rārian means to roar.
items.cn: rārian 意为吼叫。

items.en: The sound stays tied to lions and beasts.
items.cn: 这个声音一直与狮子和野兽相连。

items.en: People and crowds begin to roar too.
items.cn: 人和人群也开始「吼叫」。

items.en: Engines and traffic roar in cities.
items.cn: 城市里发动机与车流轰鸣。

items.en: Roar with laughter becomes a set phrase.
items.cn: roar with laughter 成为固定短语。

note.en: Roar is deep and long; shout is human and shorter.
note.cn: roar 低沉悠长，shout 是人的较短喊声。

entries.definition: to shout in a deep voice
to make a loud rolling sound

normalIntro.en: Roar is the sound that fills a whole valley.
normalIntro.cn: roar 是能填满整个山谷的声音。

normal.en: A lion roars across the dark plain.
normal.cn: a lion roars 狮子在黑暗平原上吼叫。

normal.en: Roar with laughter means laugh very loudly.
normal.cn: roar with laughter 意为放声大笑。

normal.en: The crowd's roar filled the stadium.
normal.cn: the roar of the crowd 填满体育场。

normal.en: To roar at someone is to shout angrily.
normal.cn: roar at 某人是愤怒地吼叫。

normal.en: A truck can roar past a quiet house.
normal.cn: 卡车会轰鸣着驶过安静的房屋。

abstract.en: Picture a lion's breath in cold night air.
abstract.cn: 想象寒夜里狮子的吐息。

abstract.en: Imagine a wave of sound hitting a stone wall.
abstract.cn: 想象声浪撞上石墙。

abstract.en: Think of engines growling like distant beasts.
abstract.cn: 想象引擎像远处野兽般低吼。

examples.en: The wind roared through the trees.
examples.cn: 风穿过树林呼啸。

examples.en: The audience roared with approval.
examples.cn: 观众大声叫好。

examples.en: We could not hear over the roar of the water.
examples.cn: 水声轰鸣，我们听不清。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「roar」听起来像「吼儿」——张开嘴吼出来的声音，就是咆哮。

root: 古英语 rārian（吼叫）→ roar，核心义「低沉、长久、充满空间的声音」，从兽吼扩展到人声与机器。

sensesIntro.en: Roar means a beast's deep cry, a human shout, or a loud machine noise.
sensesIntro.cn: roar 指野兽的低吼、人的大喊，或机器的轰鸣。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sound filling a whole valley.
core.cn: 核心意象：填满整个山谷的声音。

branches.en: The beast cry is the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 兽吼是最古老的义项。

branches.en: Angry people borrow the beast sound.
branches.cn: 愤怒的人借用了野兽的声音。

branches.en: Engines take the same deep noise.
branches.cn: 引擎也发出同样的低沉巨响。

branches.en: Beast and human both fill the air with sound.
branches.cn: 野兽与人都会用声音充满空气。

branches.en: Machines in the dark sound like animals.
branches.cn: 黑暗中的机器听起来像动物。

intro.en: Roar is a native English verb from Old English rārian.
intro.cn: roar 是源自古英语 rārian 的英语本族动词。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, with no Latin prefix.
latinIntro.cn: 该词属于日耳曼语，没有拉丁前缀。

items.example: The phrase widens the sound to joy.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语把声音扩展到欢乐。

definition_en: to cook with dry heat, roasted meat, or to tease someone publicly
core_image: 烤箱里慢慢转动的整只鸡
scene: 厨房里，父亲把整只鸡放进烤箱，让它慢慢烤。In the kitchen, father put the whole chicken in the oven to roast slowly.
sceneCN: 这里 roast 是「烤」（第 1 个义项：用干热烹制食物）；句意：厨房里，父亲把整只鸡放进烤箱，让它慢慢烤。

senses.title: Cooking with dry heat
senses.definition: to cook food with dry heat in an oven or over fire
senses.definitionCN: 在烤箱中或用火以干热烹调食物
senses.example: Roast the nuts for ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 把坚果烤十分钟。
senses.why: Dry heat browns and deepens the food.
senses.whyCN: 干热让食物上色并加深风味。

senses.title: Roasted meat
senses.definition: a piece of meat cooked in dry heat
senses.example: The Sunday roast was wonderful.
senses.exampleCN: 周日的烤肉大餐棒极了。
senses.why: The noun names what the oven has made.
senses.whyCN: 名词指烤箱做出来的东西。

senses.title: Teasing in public
senses.definition: to criticize or joke about someone in a friendly or comic way
senses.definitionCN: 以友好或滑稽的方式公开批评、打趣某人
senses.example: The show roasted a famous actor.
senses.exampleCN: 这档节目公开调侃了一位著名演员。
senses.why: Comedy heat teases without burning.
senses.whyCN: 喜剧的火候，调侃而不灼伤。

intro.en: Roast comes from Old French rostir, to roast.
intro.cn: roast 源自古法语 rostir，意为烤。

items.en: Rostir means to roast over fire.
items.cn: rostir 意为在火上烤。

items.en: Roast enters English as a cooking verb.
items.cn: roast 以烹饪动词之意进入英语。

items.en: The noun names a joint of meat.
items.cn: 名词指一大块烤肉。

items.en: Roast extends to coffee and nuts.
items.cn: roast 扩展到咖啡与坚果。

items.en: The comic roast gives a joking sense.
items.cn: 喜剧调侃节目赋予它开玩笑的义项。

note.en: Roast uses dry heat; boil uses water.
note.cn: roast 用干热，boil 用水。

entries.definition: a pan or machine for roasting
to cook under or over strong heat

normalIntro.en: To roast is to let dry heat do the work.
normalIntro.cn: roast 就是让干热来完成工作。

normal.en: Roast beef is a classic Sunday dish.
normal.cn: roast beef 是经典的周日菜肴。

normal.en: Roast chicken fills the kitchen with smell.
normal.cn: roast chicken 让厨房充满香味。

normal.en: Roast potatoes turn golden in the oven.
normal.cn: roast potatoes 在烤箱里变成金黄。

normal.en: A Sunday roast brings the family together.
normal.cn: a Sunday roast 让一家人聚在一起。

normal.en: To roast a friend is to tease them kindly.
normal.cn: roast 朋友就是善意地打趣。

abstract.en: Picture a chicken turning slowly above coals.
abstract.cn: 想象一只鸡在炭火上慢慢转动。

abstract.en: Imagine the kitchen warm and full of steam.
abstract.cn: 想象厨房温暖、蒸汽弥漫。

abstract.en: Think of a comedian's gentle fire on stage.
abstract.cn: 想象喜剧演员在台上燃起的温和之火。

examples.en: We roasted vegetables for dinner.
examples.cn: 我们烤了蔬菜当晚餐。

examples.en: He ordered the roast with potatoes.
examples.cn: 他点了烤肉配土豆。

examples.en: The comic roasted the whole team.
examples.cn: 这位喜剧演员把整支队伍都调侃了一遍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「roast」听起来像「热死它」——用热力把它烘透，就是烤。

root: 古法语 rostir（在火上烤）→ roast，核心义「用干热使食物变熟上色」，再引申出公开「烤」人的调侃义。

sensesIntro.en: Roast means to cook with dry heat, the meat so cooked, or to tease someone publicly.
sensesIntro.cn: roast 意为用干热烹调、这样烤出的肉，或公开调侃某人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: dry heat browning food.
core.cn: 核心意象：干热让食物上色。

branches.en: Cooking with dry heat is the core sense.
branches.cn: 干热烹制是核心义项。

branches.en: The noun names the finished meat.
branches.cn: 名词指烤好的肉。

branches.en: Comic teasing borrows the heat image.
branches.cn: 喜剧调侃借用了热度意象。

branches.en: The verb and its product share one word.
branches.cn: 动作与其产物共用一个词。

branches.en: Both real fire and comic fire need good control.
branches.cn: 真实的火与喜剧的火都需要掌控火候。

intro.en: Roast is a French borrowing from rostir.
intro.cn: roast 是来自 rostir 的法语借词。

latinIntro.en: The French verb is its direct parent.
latinIntro.cn: 法语动词是它的直接来源。

items.exampleCN: 这个复合词指一种传统。

definition_en: to steal from a person or place, or to take something away unfairly
core_image: 深夜被撬开的后门
scene: 深夜，两名男子撬开商店后门行窃。Two men broke in through the back door and robbed the shop.
sceneCN: 这里 rob 是「抢劫」（第 1 个义项：从人或场所夺走财物）；句意：深夜，两名男子撬开商店后门行窃。

senses.title: Stealing by force
senses.definition: to take money or property from a person or place
senses.definitionCN: 从人或场所夺走钱财或财物
senses.example: They robbed the shop at midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 他们半夜抢劫了这家店。
senses.why: The verb targets the place or person, not the thing.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词的宾语是人或场所，而不是财物。

senses.title: Taking away unfairly
senses.definition: to take something valuable away from someone
senses.definitionCN: 从某人那里夺走珍贵的东西
senses.example: Illness robbed him of his hearing.
senses.exampleCN: 疾病夺走了他的听力。
senses.why: Loss can feel like a theft by life itself.
senses.whyCN: 失去感觉就像被生活本身偷走。

intro.en: Rob comes from Old French rober, to plunder.
intro.cn: rob 源自古法语 rober，意为掠夺。

items.en: Rober means to plunder.
items.cn: rober 意为掠夺。

items.en: Rob enters English as a verb of theft.
items.cn: rob 以盗窃动词进入英语。

items.en: Robber and robbery grow beside it.
items.cn: robber 与 robbery 随之产生。

items.en: Rob someone of something means deprive.
items.cn: rob someone of something 意为剥夺。

items.en: Legal use keeps robbery as a serious crime.
items.cn: 法律用语中 robbery 是重罪。

note.en: You rob a person or place; you steal a thing.
note.cn: rob 的宾语是人或场所，steal 的宾语是物品。

entries.definition: to take something that is not yours

normalIntro.en: To rob is to take from a person or a place.
normalIntro.cn: rob 就是从人或场所夺走东西。

normal.en: Rob a bank means take its money.
normal.cn: rob a bank 意为抢走银行的钱。

normal.en: Rob someone of sleep means keep them awake.
normal.cn: rob someone of sleep 意为让人无法入睡。

normal.en: A robber is the person who robs.
normal.cn: a robber 就是实施 rob 的人。

normal.en: Robbery is the crime itself.
normal.cn: robbery 是抢劫罪行本身。

normal.en: Remember: rob a place, steal a thing.
normal.cn: 记住：rob 接场所，steal 接物品。

abstract.en: Picture a back door swinging open in the dark.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗中后门被推开。

abstract.en: Imagine a hand pulling a wallet from a pocket.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手从口袋里抽走钱包。

abstract.en: Think of a shadow running with a heavy bag.
abstract.cn: 想象一个影子提着沉重的袋子奔跑。

examples.en: Someone robbed the old man on the bus.
examples.cn: 有人在公交车上抢了这位老人的东西。

examples.en: The war robbed the town of its young people.
examples.cn: 战争夺走了这座小镇的年轻人。

examples.en: They were robbed while on holiday.
examples.cn: 他们度假时被抢了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rob」听起来像「落不」——东西落到手里就不还，就是抢。

root: 古法语 rober（掠夺）→ rob，核心义「用强力从人或场所夺走财物」，引申为剥夺珍贵之物。

sensesIntro.en: Rob means to steal from a person or place, or to deprive someone of something valuable.
sensesIntro.cn: rob 意为从人或场所抢走财物，或剥夺某人珍贵的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a back door forced open.
core.cn: 核心意象：被强行撬开的后门。

branches.en: Taking from a person or place is the core.
branches.cn: 从人或场所夺取是核心义。

branches.en: Deprivation extends theft beyond money.
branches.cn: 剥夺把盗窃延伸到钱财之外。

branches.en: Both theft and loss leave someone emptier.
branches.cn: 偷窃与失去都让人变得更空。

branches.en: Robbery turns the act into a named crime.
branches.cn: robbery 把这一行为变成有名称的罪行。

branches.en: Illness can rob without any thief.
branches.cn: 疾病也能在没有窃贼的情况下夺走东西。

intro.en: Rob is a French borrowing from rober, to plunder.
intro.cn: rob 是来自 rober（掠夺）的法语借词。

latinIntro.en: Old French rober is the direct source.
latinIntro.cn: 古法语 rober 是直接来源。

items.example: The phrase adds the sense of loss.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语增加失去的含义。

definition_en: a large stone, to move gently back and forth, or rock music
core_image: 海浪拍打的岸边岩石
scene: 海浪不断拍打着岸边的岩石。Waves kept beating against the rocks on the shore.
sceneCN: 这里 rock 是「岩石」（第 1 个义项：大块坚硬的石头）；句意：海浪不断拍打着岸边的岩石。

senses.title: A large stone
senses.definition: a large hard mass of stone
senses.example: A grey rock stood at the path's end.
senses.exampleCN: 小路尽头立着一块灰色岩石。
senses.why: The solid stone is the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 坚实的石头是最古老的义项。

senses.title: Moving gently
senses.definition: to move gently from side to side
senses.example: She rocked the child to sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 她轻摇孩子入睡。
senses.why: The cradle repeats a slow side-to-side motion.
senses.whyCN: 摇篮重复着缓慢的左右摆动。

senses.title: Rock music
senses.definition: a loud popular music with strong beat
senses.definitionCN: 节奏强劲的响亮流行音乐
senses.example: The band plays old rock.
senses.exampleCN: 这支乐队演奏老摇滚。
senses.why: The music took the name of its rolling beat.
senses.whyCN: 这种音乐沿用了它翻滚般节奏的名字。

intro.en: Rock comes from Old French roche, from Medieval Latin rocca, a crag.
intro.cn: rock 源自古法语 roche，来自中世纪拉丁语 rocca（岩崖）。

items.en: Rocca means a crag or rock.
items.cn: rocca 意为岩崖或岩石。

items.en: Old French roche carries the stone sense.
items.cn: 古法语 roche 保留石头义。

items.en: Rock names stone, then a gentle sway.
items.cn: rock 先指石头，后指轻摇。

items.en: Rock music rises in the mid twentieth century.
items.cn: 摇滚乐在二十世纪中叶兴起。

items.en: Rock and roll links the sway and the sound.
items.cn: rock and roll 把摇摆与声音联系起来。

note.en: A rock is big and solid; a stone is smaller.
note.cn: rock 是大而坚实的石块，stone 通常更小。

entries.definition: a rocking chair or rock musician
to move slowly side to side

normalIntro.en: Rock is stone, a sway, and a rolling beat.
normalIntro.cn: rock 既是石头，也是摇摆，还是一种翻滚的节奏。

normal.en: A large rock blocks the narrow path.
normal.cn: a large rock 堵住了狭窄的小路。

normal.en: Rock the baby gently in your arms.
normal.cn: rock the baby 就是在怀里轻轻摇晃婴儿。

normal.en: Rock climbing needs strong hands.
normal.cn: rock climbing 需要有力的双手。

normal.en: Solid rock is hard to dig through.
normal.cn: solid rock 很难挖穿。

normal.en: Rock music has a strong beat.
normal.cn: rock music 节奏强劲。

abstract.en: Picture waves striking a grey shore rock.
abstract.cn: 想象海浪拍打灰色的岸边岩石。

abstract.en: Imagine a cradle swinging in a quiet room.
abstract.cn: 想象安静房间里摆动的摇篮。

abstract.en: Think of a stage shaking with a heavy beat.
abstract.cn: 想象舞台随沉重节拍震动。

examples.en: The boat hit a rock near the shore.
examples.cn: 小船在岸边撞上了岩石。

examples.en: He rocked the chair back and forth.
examples.cn: 他让椅子前后摇晃。

examples.en: They listened to rock all night.
examples.cn: 他们整夜听摇滚乐。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rock」听起来像「落磕」——从山上落下来磕人的硬块，就是岩石。

root: 中世纪拉丁语 rocca（岩崖）→ 古法语 roche → rock，核心义「坚硬的大石」，再由摇篮的摆动引申出摇动与摇滚乐。

sensesIntro.en: Rock means a large stone, a gentle swaying motion, or rock music.
sensesIntro.cn: rock 意为大块岩石、轻轻摇动，或摇滚乐。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grey stone in moving waves.
core.cn: 核心意象：波浪中的灰色岩石。

branches.en: The stone is the oldest noun sense.
branches.cn: 石头是最古老的名词义项。

branches.en: The gentle sway is the verb sense.
branches.cn: 轻摇是动词义项。

branches.en: Rock music takes the rolling beat.
branches.cn: 摇滚乐沿用了翻滚的节拍。

branches.en: Even a heavy rock can rock in an earthquake.
branches.cn: 连沉重的岩石也会在地震中摇晃。

branches.en: The cradle sway and the music beat share motion.
branches.cn: 摇篮摆动与音乐节拍都共享运动感。

intro.en: Rock descends from Old French roche, a crag.
intro.cn: rock 源自古法语 roche（岩崖）。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin rocca is the earliest known form.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 rocca 是目前已知最早的形式。

items.example: Rocker names a chair or player.
The phrase joins sway and music.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语把摇摆与音乐连在一起。

latinEntries.example: Rocca is the source of rock.
latinEntries.exampleCN: rocca 是 rock 的来源。

definition_en: a vehicle or firework driven upward by burning fuel, or to rise very fast
core_image: 拖着白烟冲向天空的火箭
scene: 倒计时结束，火箭拖着白烟冲向天空。The countdown ended and the rocket shot into the sky.
sceneCN: 这里 rocket 是「火箭」（第 1 个义项：靠燃烧燃料升空的飞行器）；句意：倒计时结束，火箭拖着白烟冲向天空。

senses.title: A space vehicle
senses.definition: a vehicle driven upward by burning fuel
senses.definitionCN: 靠燃烧燃料向上推进的飞行器
senses.example: The rocket carried a small satellite.
senses.exampleCN: 这枚火箭运载了一颗小卫星。
senses.why: Burning fuel pushes the craft against gravity.
senses.whyCN: 燃烧的燃料把飞行器推向重力之上。

senses.title: A firework or signal
senses.definition: a firework that shoots up or a warning flare
senses.definitionCN: 冲上天空的烟火或警示信号弹
senses.example: A red rocket marked the start of the race.
senses.exampleCN: 一枚红色信号弹标志着比赛开始。
senses.why: The old firework is a small rocket.
senses.whyCN: 古老的烟火就是一枝小火箭。

senses.title: Rising fast
senses.definition: to increase or move upward very quickly
senses.definitionCN: 非常迅速地增长或向上移动
senses.example: House prices rocketed last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 去年春天房价飞涨。
senses.why: A rocket's climb becomes a picture of speed.
senses.whyCN: 火箭的爬升成为速度的图景。

intro.en: Rocket comes from Italian rocchetta, a small spindle, from the firework's shape.
intro.cn: rocket 源自意大利语 rocchetta（小纺锤），因烟火形状得名。

items.en: Rocca means a distaff or spindle.
items.cn: rocca 意为纺锤杆。

items.en: Rocchetta is a small spindle.
items.cn: rocchetta 是小纺锤。

items.en: French roquette names a firework.
items.cn: 法语 roquette 指一种烟火。

items.en: Rocket first means a firework.
items.cn: rocket 最初指烟火。

items.en: It becomes a vehicle for space travel.
items.cn: 它成为太空旅行的飞行器。

note.en: A rocket is powered; a missile is a weapon; a spacecraft carries people or cargo.
note.cn: rocket 是动力飞行器，missile 是武器，spacecraft 载人或载货。

entries.definition: a weapon sent through the air
a vehicle for travel in space
to rise quickly through the air

normalIntro.en: A rocket was once a firework shaped like a spindle.
normalIntro.cn: rocket 最初是一种纺锤形的烟火。

normal.en: A rocket launch shakes the ground.
normal.cn: rocket launch 震动地面。

normal.en: A space rocket leaves the atmosphere.
normal.cn: space rocket 飞出大气层。

normal.en: Rocket science means a hard subject.
normal.cn: rocket science 意为高深的学问。

normal.en: Prices rocket when demand is high.
normal.cn: 需求高时 prices rocket 价格飞涨。

normal.en: Rocket into space means travel upward fast.
normal.cn: rocket into space 意为快速飞向太空。

abstract.en: Picture a white trail cutting the blue sky.
abstract.cn: 想象一道白烟切开蓝天。

abstract.en: Imagine a small firework hissing up in the dark.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚小烟火在黑暗中嘶嘶上升。

abstract.en: Think of a price chart climbing like a launched craft.
abstract.cn: 想象价格曲线像发射的飞行器般攀升。

examples.en: The rocket lifted off at dawn.
examples.cn: 火箭在黎明时发射升空。

examples.en: A warning rocket lit the night sky.
examples.cn: 一枚警示信号弹照亮夜空。

examples.en: Demand for the new phone rocketed.
examples.cn: 新款手机的需求猛增。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rocket」听起来像「绕可特」——绕开地面、冲得特别快，就是火箭。

root: 意大利语 rocca（纺锤杆）→ rocchetta（小纺锤）→ 烟火 → rocket，再由「冲天」引申为飞速上升。

sensesIntro.en: A rocket is a space vehicle or firework, and to rocket is to rise very fast.
sensesIntro.cn: rocket 指太空飞行器或烟火，作动词表示飞速上升。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white trail cutting the sky.
core.cn: 核心意象：划开天空的一道白烟。

branches.en: The space vehicle is the main modern sense.
branches.cn: 太空飞行器是主要的现代义项。

branches.en: The firework keeps the oldest use.
branches.cn: 烟火保留了最古老的用法。

branches.en: The verb pictures a rocket's climb.
branches.cn: 动词描绘火箭般的爬升。

branches.en: Both the toy firework and the giant craft fly up.
branches.cn: 小烟火与巨型飞行器都会升空。

branches.en: Prices and rockets both shoot upward.
branches.cn: 价格与火箭都向上猛冲。

intro.en: Rocket comes from Italian rocchetta, a small spindle.
intro.cn: rocket 来自意大利语 rocchetta（小纺锤）。

latinIntro.en: The spindle shape named the firework and then the vehicle.
latinIntro.cn: 纺锤形状先给烟火命名，再给飞行器命名。

items.example: Rocket entered English as a firework.
items.exampleCN: rocket 以烟火之意进入英语。
